summary: The quote latency degradation on trading screens is best explained by loss of the quote:<n> keys in the shared redis-cache, which triggered a cache-miss storm at market-data-service and cascaded deadline-exceeded errors into pricing-engine (H1, confidence 0.60 — above threshold and clearly ahead of H2 0.30 and H3 0.22). The chain is directly observed at both ends: market-data-service began emitting "cache miss storm: quote:<n> not in redis-cache, rebuilding from exchange feed snapshot" WARNs at 13:22:25Z, coincident with pricing-engine's p99 step from ~61ms to ~2225ms at 13:22Z, and pricing-engine's 192 errors all attribute the timeout to market-data-service with no accompanying CPU/memory/load change on pricing-engine itself. The change inventory is empty at every scope checked (no pricing-engine, redis-cache, market-data-service, org-wide, or config/flag change in or around the window), ruling out the deployment/config hypotheses. Confidence is medium rather than high because the cache-side mechanism (eviction vs TTL expiry vs silent failover) could not be observed — no redis-cache telemetry was retrieved — and market-data-service's own p99 could not be measured; H3, a silent infra event on the redis host, remains a live alternative with the same visible signature.

ranked_hypotheses.title: redis-cache key loss (eviction/TTL/failover) triggers cache-miss storm at market-data-service, cascading deadline-exceeded into pricing-engine
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The shared redis-cache lost the quote:<n> keys (eviction under maxmemory, TTL expiry, or a silent primary failover promoting an empty replica). market-data-service then had to rebuild every quote from the exchange feed snapshot, its per-call latency rose to seconds, and pricing-engine's synchronous http call to market-data-service exceeded its deadline, producing 2-3s quote loads on trading screens. No code or config change was involved; the origin is the cache layer.

market-data-service sees 'cache miss storm: quote:<n> not in redis-cache, rebuilding from exchange feed snapshot', starting 13:22:25Z, 289 WARN lines
Rebuilds from the exchange feed are slow, so market-data-service call latencies rise (earliest quote slowdown 6864ms)

pricing-engine's synchronous call to market-data-service breaches its deadline: 192 ERRORs 'quote computation deadline exceeded: market-data-service took <n>ms', per-call 827-8456ms, first at 13:23:57Z
pricing-engine p99 steps from ~60ms to >2000ms at the 13:20-13:22Z boundary and never recovers
Trading screens (via order-service/api-gateway) show 2-3s slow quotes

assumptions: The redis-cache key loss is real and unexplained by any recorded change; no telemetry from redis-cache (evictions, expired_keys, maxmemory, hit/miss ratio, failover) was retrieved, so the mechanism behind the miss storm is inferred not observed.
market-data-service's own latency step matches 13:22Z (query_metrics for its p99 failed, tc-013), so its degradation is inferred from log payloads rather than measured.

The miss storm is not merely a symptom of an even earlier upstream (exchange-gateway) failure -- exchange-gateway is only reached during the rebuild fallback, but its own health in the window is unverified.

The origin should be localised to the market-data-service/redis-cache path; the fix would be there (cache warm/repair or market-data-service fallback), not in pricing-engine.
